description: The principles, laws and engineering practices that keep personal data safe and lawfully used, from consent and impact assessments to anonymisation and privacy-aware database design. Students work through branching compliance cases and build and attack small datasets in the lab.
modelledOn: Cavoukian, Privacy by Design: The 7 Foundational Principles
Dwork and Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy (introductory chapters)
IAPP Certified Information Privacy Professional body of knowledge
outcomes: Classify data as personal, sensitive or anonymous and apply the core privacy principles to a described system.
Compare the Ghana Data Protection Act with other African and international laws and decide which obligations apply to a case.
Carry out a privacy impact assessment with a data-flow map, a risk rating and justified mitigations.
Anonymise and pseudonymise a dataset, measure its k-anonymity and attack it with a linkage test.
Handle consent, data subject requests and a personal data breach within the legal time limits.
Design a database schema and access model that applies data minimisation, retention and audit logging.

units.title: Personal data and privacy principles
topics: Concepts of privacy: information, bodily and decisional privacy; contextual integrity
Personal data, identifiability, and special categories: health, biometric, financial and children's data
Fair information practice principles: collection limitation, purpose specification, use limitation, data quality, openness
Roles: data controller, data processor, data subject, regulator and data protection officer
Privacy harms and threats: profiling, surveillance, SIM registration, digital ID and mobile money trails

units.title: Data protection legislation in practice
topics: Structure of the Ghana Data Protection Act 2012 and the work of the Data Protection Commission
Lawful bases for processing: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital and legitimate interests
Comparison of GDPR, POPIA, the Kenya Data Protection Act and the Nigeria Data Protection Act
Cross-border transfers, adequacy decisions, standard contractual clauses and data localisation
Accountability: registration, records of processing, penalties and enforcement case studies

units.title: Privacy impact assessments
topics: When a data protection impact assessment is required and who must sign it off
Data-flow mapping: sources, stores, recipients, retention and transfers
Risk assessment: likelihood, severity, risk matrices and residual risk
Selecting and documenting mitigations; consulting the regulator
Processor and vendor due diligence, data processing agreements and audits

units.title: Anonymisation and pseudonymisation
topics: Direct and quasi-identifiers; linkage attacks and famous re-identification cases
k-anonymity by generalisation and suppression; information loss measures
l-diversity, t-closeness and the homogeneity and background-knowledge attacks
Pseudonymisation: tokenisation, keyed hashing, salting, and why plain hashing fails
Differential privacy: the Laplace mechanism, epsilon, sensitivity and composition; synthetic data

units.title: Consent and data subject rights
topics: Valid consent: freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous; withdrawal; dark patterns
Rights of access, rectification, objection and restriction
Erasure and portability; handling a data subject request workflow with identity checks and deadlines
Special cases: children, health data, employee data, credit reporting and direct marketing
Retention schedules and secure deletion across backups and processors

units.title: Breach notification and response
topics: What counts as a personal data breach: confidentiality, integrity and availability loss
Detection, triage and severity scoring; the first 72 hours
Notification duties: regulator, data subjects, timelines and content of a notice
Containment, evidence preservation, root cause and post-incident review
Case studies of telecom, fintech and health-sector breaches in Africa and a tabletop exercise

units.title: Privacy by design in databases
topics: The seven foundational principles of privacy by design and data minimisation in schema design
Separating identifiers from attributes; vertical partitioning and lookup keys
Encryption in transit, at rest and at field level; key management and rotation
Access control: roles, views, row-level security and audit logging of reads
Privacy-preserving analytics: aggregation thresholds, query auditing and purpose limitation checks

units.title: Governance, emerging technology and privacy audit
topics: Privacy programme: policies, training, privacy notices and metrics
Machine learning and privacy: membership inference, model inversion and biometric systems
Digital ID, mobile money, telemedicine and CCTV: sector-specific privacy risks
Privacy-enhancing technologies: secure multiparty computation, homomorphic encryption and federated learning
Privacy audit of a mobile money application: findings, ratings and remediation plan

schedule.title: Privacy concepts and personal data
schedule.exercise: Classify twenty data fields from a clinic registration form as personal, special category or non-personal, and map each to the principle it most affects.

tasks.title: Sort 15 data fields from a pharmacy app into personal, sensitive or non-personal and justify each choice in the scenario rubric
Review a school fee app's data practices and identify which fair information principles it breaks, citing the evidence in the case file
Judge three data flows in a smart-city case using contextual integrity and decide which flows violate the norms of their original context

schedule.title: Roles, harms and threat landscape
schedule.exercise: Draw a role diagram for a mobile money transfer naming controller, processor and data subject, then list three privacy harms that follow from the data trail it leaves.

tasks.title: Draw a diagram of a ride-hailing app labelling each party as controller, joint controller, processor or data subject
Work through a SIM registration case, rank six privacy harms by severity and propose one safeguard for each of the top three
Resolve a dispute between a hospital, a cloud vendor and an analytics firm by assigning controller and processor duties and defending the allocation

schedule.title: Data protection law across jurisdictions
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page comparison table of the Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa and EU laws covering lawful bases, transfer rules, registration and penalties.

tasks.title: Pick the correct lawful basis for eight processing activities of a bank and record the clause that supports each
Decide whether a Ghanaian fintech may store customer records on a European cloud region and list the safeguards needed for the transfer
Act as the regulator on a complaint against a telecom and choose between warning, order and fine, justifying each against the evidence and statute

schedule.title: Running a data protection impact assessment
schedule.exercise: Complete a DPIA template for a community health worker app: describe the processing, map the data flows, rate the risks and agree mitigations.

tasks.title: Draw a data-flow diagram for a loan app showing sources, stores, third-party recipients and retention period on each flow
Rate ten privacy risks in a payroll system on a likelihood and severity matrix and choose the top three for mitigation
Audit three candidate analytics vendors from their contracts, rank them by privacy risk and draft the five clauses a processing agreement must contain

schedule.title: Re-identification and k-anonymity
schedule.exercise: Take a table of 30 patients and generalise age and postcode until it is 3-anonymous, then explain what a homogeneity attack could still reveal.

tasks.title: Join a released health table to a public voter list on postcode, birth year and sex and count how many people become unique
Write a function that checks k-anonymity of a small table and generalise age into bands until k reaches 3 with minimum information loss
Measure l-diversity and t-closeness on an anonymised disease table, then mount a homogeneity attack on one equivalence class and report what leaks

schedule.title: Pseudonymisation and differential privacy
schedule.exercise: Show why an unsalted hash of a phone number can be reversed, design a keyed pseudonym scheme, and compute the noise needed for an epsilon of 1 on a count query.

tasks.title: Hash 1,000 Ghana mobile numbers with SHA-256, then recover them by brute force to show why plain hashing is not pseudonymisation
Add Laplace noise to a count query at epsilon 0.1, 1 and 10, run 500 trials each and plot the error distribution
Build a privacy budget tracker that answers repeated queries with Laplace noise and refuses once the total epsilon is spent

schedule.title: Consent and the rights of data subjects
schedule.exercise: Redesign a consent screen for a mobile lending app so it is specific and unbundled, and write the response steps for an access request and an erasure request.

tasks.title: Review five consent screens and mark each valid or invalid against the four tests, noting which dark pattern appears
Process an erasure request from a customer of an online shop, deciding which records must be deleted and which may be kept by law
Write SQL that exports one person's data across four tables as a portable file and a second script that erases it while keeping audit rows

schedule.title: Special cases and retention
schedule.exercise: Draft a retention schedule for a campus clinic covering patient notes, appointment logs and CCTV, with a deletion method for each.

tasks.title: Match ten record types from a school to the right retention period and say which must be destroyed at the end of it
Decide whether a hospital may share a child's records with a researcher and a parent, using the case evidence and consent rules
Schedule a retention job on a Linux server that deletes expired records, rotates logs and records proof of deletion for the audit trail

schedule.title: Responding to a personal data breach
schedule.exercise: Write a breach notification to the regulator and a plain-language notice to customers for a stolen laptop holding 4,000 loan records.

tasks.title: Classify six incidents as confidentiality, integrity or availability breaches and decide which count as reportable personal data breaches
Triage a leaked database incident, score its severity and choose containment steps within the first 72 hours of the scenario clock
Lead a tabletop exercise for a mobile money breach, balancing regulator notice, customer notice and evidence preservation, and score the decisions

schedule.title: Minimising data in schema and storage
schedule.exercise: Redesign a student records schema so identifiers sit in one table, sensitive columns are encrypted, and each analytics table holds only what it needs.

tasks.title: Remove every column from a customer table that the stated purpose does not need and justify each removal
Split a patient table into an identity table and a clinical table linked by a random key and show that reports still run
Implement field-level encryption for a national ID column with key rotation and prove old rows still decrypt after the key changes

schedule.title: Access control, audit and private analytics
schedule.exercise: Create roles for nurse, billing clerk and researcher on a clinic database and write the views that give each only the fields and rows they may see.

tasks.title: Create a view that hides the national ID and phone number columns and grant a researcher role access to it only
Add an audit table and trigger that logs every read of patient rows by user and time, then query who looked at one record
Write a query guard that rejects aggregate queries on groups smaller than 5 and show a differencing attack that tries to get around it

schedule.title: Governance, AI and sector risks
schedule.exercise: Prepare a half-page privacy notice and a staff training outline for a telemedicine start-up, and list the privacy risks of its symptom-checking model.

tasks.title: Rewrite a privacy notice full of legal jargon into plain language and check it against the required content list
Run a membership inference test on a small overfitted classifier and report how well the attacker tells training rows from unseen rows
Simulate federated averaging across three clinics without sharing raw records and compare accuracy and exposure against a centralised model

schedule.title: Privacy audit capstone
schedule.exercise: Audit a described mobile money application against the law and the privacy by design principles and present a findings table with ratings and fixes.

tasks.title: Complete the audit checklist for a mobile money app case and mark each control as met, partly met or missing with evidence
Draw the data-flow diagram of a digital ID enrolment system and mark the three points of highest privacy risk
Deliver a full audit of a telemedicine platform: findings, severity ratings, regulator exposure and a costed remediation plan, scored on the rubric
